utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-14-R77.6, the Prosecutor versus Domagoj Margetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The trial was scheduled to start at this very moment. Nevertheless, the Chamber has decided that we'll first, before the trial starts, have a brief hearing on an outstanding matter in relation to witness protection where the Chamber earlier decided that it would hear the Defence first before taking any decision. For that reason, we now turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We've now come at the point that the trial in this case will start. The Chamber has in mind to proceed in the following way: First to hear brief opening statements from Prosecution and Defence, perhaps followed by a few questions by the Chamber to verify whether we have understood exactly what the Prosecution, what the Defence case is, then put some additional questions on the basis of the opening statements to explore whether there are any facts not in dispute so that we could proceed without paying attention to it in presentation of evidence, and to then proceed to the presentation of the Prosecution's case and later hear the evidence the Defence would like to present. Therefore, Ms. Sutherland, I'd like to give you the opportunity to make an opening statement if you wish to make one, and I'd like to limit your time to seven minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, the essential facts in this case revolve around the accused publishing on the internet web site, www.domagojmargetic.com, the entire confidential Prosecution witness list in the case Prosecutor versus Blaskic and three articles authored by him about protective witnesses contained in the witness list. The accused disseminated to the public the identity of 48 persons who had been granted pseudonyms, 21 of which had been granted closed-session status by the Blaskic Trial Chamber. The magnitude and implications arising from such egregious conduct distinguishes this case from any other contempt case heard by the Tribunal to date. The evidence will establish beyond reasonable doubt the accused published the witness list and the first, second, and third articles on the web side www.domagojmargetic.com knowingly and wilfully in violation of orders of the Blaskic Trial Chamber and interfered with the Tribunal's witnesses. As such, he interfered with the administration of justice and should be found in contempt of this Tribunal. First, witnesses are expected to testify that they observed the witness list and the first, second and third articles on the said web site. The first article authored by the accused which accompanied the witness list clearly showed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Sutherland please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, you heard the request. I hope it's not caused by the time-limit I set. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The first article authored by the accused which accompanied the witness list clearly shows that the accused knew the material was confidential. In the article he stated: "I have decided to publish this list of protected witnesses." On the 12th of September, the accused issued an official statement on the web site www.croatianworldwideassociation.com web site wherein he stated: "I published one of the witness names in an article on my web site on July 14, 2006. Subsequently I published the entire witness list on my web site on the 23rd of July, 2006. I removed and deleted the entire witness list from my web site on August 2nd, 2006." Second, the evidence will show that the accused knew that the information disclosed was protected. The accused received the witness list from the Prosecution pursuant to its Rule 65 ter obligations in another case. The witness list consisted of two ICTY registry confidential lists and a public ICTY registry public list of the Prosecution witnesses in the Blaskic trial. Of the two confidential lists, one had a handwritten annotation in English on the first page "confidential," and the other, a handwritten annotation in English, "confidential, do not distribute." The witness list included the identities of 48 witnesses and their pseudonyms. The witness list also included the words "clos.," c-l-o-s., next to the witnesses who testified in closed session. The cover letter that accompanied the witness list received by the accused on the 16th of May, 2006 explicitly warned him that: "This material is subject to oral and written non-disclosure orders. None of this material is to be used or disclosed for any purpose not directly related to the preparation and presentation of the above-titled cases. It may not be used for any other purpose including as to any other case or proceeding at the ICTY." In the second and third articles authored by the accused, the accused acknowledged that the witnesses he was writing about enjoyed protective measures status and referred to that fact, that a number of witnesses testified in closed session under pseudonym. Evidence will show that subsequent to the publication of the witness list and the articles the accused admitted on a number of occasions that he was aware of the confidentiality of the material. On the 2nd of August, 2006, he was reported by HINA news agency as saying: "He published a list of all the protected Prosecution witnesses from the trial of Bosnian Croat General Tihomir Blaskic on his web site three weeks ago."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, when I listen to the French translation, they are quite a bit behind, so would you please give them some time to catch up and then proceed a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise to the interpreters. On the 20th of August, 2006, in a handwritten note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the 20th of August, 2006, in a handwritten note to the Zagreb County Court, the accused stated: "I give you my word and promise that I will never again disclose or in any way use confidential ICTY information." Other documentary evidence will show that the information disclosed was covered by court orders issued by the Blaskic Trial Chamber. The evidence will establish beyond reasonable doubt that by publishing the witness list the accused interfered with the administration of justice by interfering with witnesses who testified in the Blaskic case. The interference is that their lives have been significantly affected because they were witnesses before the ICTY and the disclosure of their identity promised to remain confidential has affected their willingness to cooperate with the Tribunal in the future. In fact, the violation of their protections by the accused has caused one witness to indicate that the witness no longer is willing to cooperate with the Tribunal, and two of the witnesses that they are unwilling to cooperate with national courts. By his actions and words, it is evident that the accused intended to interfere with witnesses. At a minimum, it is evident that the accused was aware of the likelihood that his disclosure of the protected identity would interfere with witnesses. With this awareness, he continued regardless thereby accepting the results. There is evidence that the publication of the witness list by the accused interfered with the witnesses. The witnesses are expected to testify that as a result of the publication they have suffered psychological harm in their lives and that of their families have been seriously affected. One witness is undergoing psychiatric treatment as a result. They live in constant fear for their safety and security and that of family members. They live in fear of repercussions for having testified against Blaskic. Their freedom of movement has been enormously curtailed. The evidence will show that the accused was aware and accepted the likelihood that -- or at least he was manifest indifferent to the repercussions which may occur from the publication of the witness list and/or that the witnesses may not be willing to cooperate with the ICTY or future judicial -- or judicial bodies in the future. The evidence will show that the accused's cavalier approach to the effect of his publication or the relevance to the people whose identity he reveals. In the first article, the accused said he would "sooner or later publish that confidential document because I have done so before. I have said that I will always and regardless of the people in question do the same, publish the information I obtained." The evidence will show that the accused carried out the intentional dissemination of the protected identities of 48 witnesses with no control or limits on the dissemination. The protected information disclosed by the accused was disseminated to a wider audience, including web sites www.011385.com and www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com. The information was either copied or hyperlinked back to the offending material on the accused's web site, www.domagojmargetic.com. Publishing information on the internet makes the information accessible to an indefinite audience and therefore greatly increases the likelihood of interference with witnesses. The evidence will finally prove that the accused's denigrating characterisation of the witnesses whose identity he chose to expose to the public. In the accused's official statement, he states: "The reason I published the witness list in part was to reveal to the world that some witnesses were in fact Mujahedin or better known to the world as terrorists. In light of the anniversary of 9/11, it is important for the public to know with whom the ICTY were working with to prosecute General Tihomir Blaskic." The Prosecution case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I gave you seven minutes. We are quite a bit beyond the seven minutes now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one sentence in conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to hear that last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Prosecution case is the oral evidence you are about to hear on the documentary evidence submitted as part of the Rule 65 ter exhibits. The evidence shows in this case will prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused knowingly and wilfully violated the orders of the Tribunal, interfered with the Tribunal's witnesses and as such the accused interfered with the administration of justice and is in contempt of this Tribunal. This completes the opening statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Mr. Miljevic, do you want to make an opening statement as well, or would you like to delay your opening statement?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can say a few introductory words. First of all, this indictment was filed on the basis of the inherent powers of this Tribunal. I have to say despite the earlier adduced positions in different other cases that my client and I feel that this Tribunal does not have jurisdiction to try cases like these; namely, I'm quite certain that the intention of Resolution 808 of the 3rd of May, 1993, and Resolution 827 of the 13th of May, 1993, whereunder this Tribunal was established and when its Statute was adopted did not foresee its jurisdiction for cases like these. I have carefully read both Resolutions, and they do not refer to what this Tribunal should by example try or predominantly try but it says expressis verbis that it is the exclusive jurisdiction of this Tribunal to try severe violations of humanitarian law in the former Yugoslavia. This is what I felt I should say in the introduction, because I believe that this Tribunal is not competent to try such cases on the basis of its inherent powers, inherent authority. Now, as regards the indictment itself, the indictment considers that my client, Domagoj Margetic, a Croatian journalist, is in breach of Rule 77(A)(i) and (A)(iv) by having disclosed a list of protected witnesses. I have to say in brief that it will not be at all in doubt that all these witnesses have under decisions of previous Trial Chambers in 1997, concretely speaking on the 10th of July and the 10th of November, 1997, acquired protective status. That is indubitable. There is no duty also that Domagoj Margetic has already been before this Tribunal and that proceedings for contempt of court had already been instituted which referred to the same list of protected witnesses. However, what will be disputable is what follows after Count 3 of the indictment, which is the 7th of -- of July, 1997. I don't know why the OTP chose that day, but by a careful examination of the documentation I found nothing of significance which happened on that particular day in relation to this legal matter. In fact, to be quite honest, I found nothing which is of relevance to this legal matter. It seems to my client and it seems to me that this date was chosen deliberately because my client still maintains, and he also maintained so in July and August of this year, that as of the 11th of July this year that list of protected witnesses was not -- has not been confidential but was in the public domain, accessible to the public. Now, whether my client maintains that with justification or misinterprets the rulings of this Court will be seen during the proceedings. It is, however, quite clear that on the 11th of July, during the trial to the accused journalist Josip Jovic this Tribunal adopted a decision on the basis of a submission by the OTP whereunder the list was published, the list of protected witnesses. My client, who is also a jurist -- who is not a jurist and only has some indirect knowledge of jurisprudence, can say that on the 7th of July nothing happened. On the 14th of July, Domagoj Margetic, on his web site www.domagojmargetic.com named a handful of witnesses who were on the list of the protected witnesses in the Blaskic trial. And between the 23rd and the 26th of July, the other articles which the OTP refers to were published. My client learned that on the 28th of July, 2006, the Prosecutor filed an ex parte and urgent motion for an order for the immediate cessation of violation of protective measures, and even before being served that motion by the county court in Zagreb my client -- yes. It will be easier for me to -- thank you. My client, the moment he learned about this motion of the 28th of July of this year he actually extinguished his web site on the 1st of August this year. My client maintained that all until the 22nd of August it had been absolutely permitted to publish that list, and it was in that conviction that apart from the fact on -- that on the 11th of July the ruling was brought in the proceeding against the Josip Jovic, and on the 22nd of August a ruling was handed down by this Tribunal which was read by Justice Patrick Robinson whereunder the list of protected witnesses was again proclaimed confidential and sealed. If this happened between the 7th of July and the 2nd of August, and my client claims that from the 11th of July to the 22nd of August this list was not at all confidential, then it is quite certain that as required by Article 77 under (A) this is something which is not applicable to him, that is, voluntary and wilful component of guilt, namely deliberate interference with justice on his part. Actually, my client acted in a quite permitted way after the 11th of July until the 1st or 2nd of August this year or at least he was -- he laboured under a justified misconception to the effect that such conduct was permitted. So what will be at issue here will be elements; namely, whether at the time of the commission of the acts that my client is charged with, whether his conduct had been disallowed at all; secondly, on what web pages was this list published; third, in whose possession are those web sites, web pages; and fourth, what are the exact dates of the publishing of the disputable materials on the internet and on the listed web sites. In responding to these precisely define questions which are also so defined in the brief of the defence of my client who only yesterday came, it will be quite clearly shown that his intention had never been to be in contempt of this court but that by publishing the disputable material in an allowed period he wanted to indicate a certain conduct on the part of the OTP of the Tribunal in The Hague. Therefore, I claim that from the 7th of July, and especially from the 11th of July this year up until the 2nd of August this year, my client performed an allowable action. If that is not so, he was quite certainly and justifiably in error of fact as to his own actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miljevic. As I said before, the Chamber might have some questions as to the -- what -- to verify whether it fully understands the Prosecution's case and the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might start with you, Ms. Sutherland. May I just find out from you, you told us in broad outline in your opening statement what the accused is alleged to have said in the second and third articles that he published. What did he say in the first?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did he say in the first article, Your Honour? That he was publishing a secret list of witnesses. He mentioned that the witnesses were protected. I can expand if you want. I can go to the exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll deal with that in evidence. I just wanted to get the theme of what he said, what he talked about in the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The title -- the title of the document is called "Exclusive list of confidential Hague witnesses given to me by Carla Del Ponte's assistant."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You also mentioned in your opening statement that the publication had the effect of interfering with the witnesses in the Blaskic case. What I do want to find out from you is, is it the Prosecution's case that the publication interfered with the Blaskic case witnesses, protected witnesses, only, or does it go beyond that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's our position that -- that his interference does go beyond the Blaskic witnesses, but the evidence that we will bring before you in this case relates to three witnesses who testified in the Blaskic case who have been -- who were the victims of -- of the disclosure. But the very fact that this information is on a web site means that when people learn about this disclosure they may well be put off testifying and cooperating with this Tribunal and/or national courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was indeed because of that statement you made also in your opening statement that I wanted to find out whether is it the Prosecution's case that it's only the witnesses in the Blaskic case or future witnesses, potential witnesses, who may be called to come and testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's also potential witnesses. But the evidence that we -- that we seek for you to hear is limited to the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could I ask one additional question then. The three witnesses you want to call or all of the witnesses on the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: All of the witnesses on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And interference with witnesses under (A)(iv) does that. Is it the Prosecution's case that you could interfere with witnesses even if they are or may not be aware of their names being published on a web site? Is it your case that you could convict for interference with, well, let's say, all the 40 witnesses, the protected witnesses, without evidence that all of these witnesses and not just three were aware of the publication?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour. If you'd give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is -- it is our position that you can interfere with witnesses even if they're not aware of their names being published on the web site, because it goes to the issue of potential witnesses who may -- who may testify in the future. We have direct evidence of -- that we wish to bring before the Chamber of three witnesses who have been interfered with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not following your argument on this point, Ms. Sutherland, because the question is: Can you interfere with witnesses who are not aware of their names being on the list. Obviously a potential witness in the future must be placed in the same position. He also has not been aware that names were put -- were published on the web site. That potential witness would not know that there had been a publication prior.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the witnesses -- the 48 witnesses that are protected. Now, if they're not aware, one of those 48 witnesses aren't aware of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The publication.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- the publication, that doesn't mean that the accused still can't be found guilty under 77(A)(iv) of interfering with witnesses who have testified and other potential witnesses, because it's other witnesses out there who read this information on the web site who may well have testified but are now because of this incident are not willing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that was not the question from Judge Orie. The question from Judge Orie was: Is it possible to be -- to be interfered with as a witness if you are not aware that your name has been published. And then you responded by saying, well, it does interfere even if you are not aware because future potential witnesses may not want to come. That's when I intervened, and I said but based on the question that a witness who's unaware of the publication of his name may or may not be interfered with, then the future potential witness must also be unaware of the publication, and the question was would the future potential witness who is unaware of the publication, can he be said to be interfered with by the publication that he's unaware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour, and the answer I think has to be no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for these clarifications, Ms. Sutherland. I'd like to explore at this moment what this case is actually about. From the questions of the Bench, Ms. Sutherland, you may have understood that one of the issues the Chamber would like to pay attention to is -- is the exact structure of 77(A)(iv), perhaps together with 77(A), the first initial paragraph. But perhaps more important the Chamber would like to explore what is in dispute as far as facts are concerned. I do understand from Mr. Miljevic that the Defence will be first of all that the disclosed list was in the public domain, that the Defence takes an issue on what web sites it was published. Third, who was the owner of these web sites. The possessor, yes. In the written material I saw ownership, but at least who was in possession of the web sites. Four, that the dates on which the material was published are relevant. And finally, the intent Mr. Margetic has had when publishing. Therefore, I'd like to see whether all the other matters are not in dispute. Mr. Miljevic, do -- does the Chamber well understand the position of the Defence that you're not challenging that Mr. Margetic published, I'm not saying yet on what web site, but did publish at any time on a web site the witness list?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I was quite clear before. We are not challenging at all that Domagoj Margetic indeed published a list of those witnesses, but in a period between the 15th of July and the 26th of July this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any dispute -- I don't think when I understood you well, there's no dispute about the fact that until, as you said, the 11th of July, and let's just keep it to that for the moment, that protective measures were in place in respect of the witnesses that appear on the list that was published by -- or was put on the web site by Mr. Margetic? The parties agree on that? Mr. Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is true. That is the demarcation line. That is what I said in my introductory comments, that the 11th of July is the date from which Domagoj Margetic thought, considered, maintained that it would be allowable conduct to publish that list. After the motion of the 28th of July by this Tribunal, he removed that list from his web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we talk about putting the within list on the internet. Also the indictment says that publications were made by Mr. Margetic. Again, I'm not talking about a time-limit, but that's not in dispute either, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what do you mean again? If you are talking about the previous proceedings, it was on the 15th of June that the motion was filed and the case was actually abandoned on the 15th of June. So I'm not sure what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is that the indictment does not only say that Mr. Margetic published a list of witnesses but also that he wrote articles in which he revealed names of witnesses. Is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in dispute, because that is not the way it is claimed in the indictment. Under number 5 in the indictment, it is said that on the 15th of July, Margetic authored and published two articles on his web site with a list that he authored his two -- that he published his own articles with a list, and this is what I'm going to prove is indisputable, that that was so. But I don't understand the meaning of again elsewhere, because this is not what the indictment claims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm just making a distinction at this moment between publishing a list and publishing an article in which names are mentioned, and that's not in dispute. I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not in dispute. Indeed, on the 15th of July two articles were published, and it is true that one should make a distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've now explored what seems to be in dispute, that is, when the publications took place, whether that was, as the indictment says, on or about the 7th of July, or as the Defence claims, after the 11th of July. Still in issue is what web sites, and one of the issues is the possession of the web site. May I ask you, Mr. Miljevic, possession of the web site, to what extent is that relevant? I mean, if I publish something on someone else's web site, would that make any difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wouldn't make any significant difference. Indeed, you're right to intervene this way. However, Croatian law does distinguish between possession and ownership. So we will see in whose possession the web page was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the issue is the following: Let's assume that Mr. Margetic published on the web site of a multinational the same information. Would that make any difference for the charges brought against him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, basically no, but then the Prosecution cannot persist in using this term that they use in the indictment all the time. I counted the number of times that they used this wording, that he published this on his web site. It is due to this terminology used by the Prosecution that I said what I said, but otherwise you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think from what I've seen on the filed materials that it's not only the Prosecution that uses that terminology but that Mr. Margetic in his own submissions says -- talks about "my web site." But that's evidence. We'll look at that later, whether -- to what extent we need to hear evidence on that, to what extent it is relevant in the context of this case. Then finally you said you'd like to prove that Mr. Margetic had no intent to disrespect the Tribunal. To what extent is that relevant? I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is relevant because the basic features of the charges brought against my client from Rule 77(A), that means that this is constituted only if a person does this wilfully and in full awareness. My witness -- my client stresses that he never wilfully wished to commit any kind of contempt of this Court. He simply wanted to indicate certain impermissible or erroneous acts on the part of the Office of the Prosecutor, not the court, not by any means. That is why he wrote this book which his Defence has given and wishes to have put in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The issue might be whether the rule requires wilful behaviour in terms of the publication of lists of witnesses. So whether it is a matter of intent or whether it's a matter of motive. Motive might be important, rather, for sentencing than for -- for the question whether the offence has been committed. We've now focused on what seems to be in dispute --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, the Prosecution will have an opportunity now to present its case, to present evidence to the Court, and we'll decide on the protective measures of MC2 and 3 after we have heard the evidence you present without any problems in relation to protective measures. Please keep in mind that a lot of issues seem not to be in dispute anymore. Is it clear to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just if I can go back to Your Honour's question about the interfering with witnesses who are not aware of the identity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And specifically interference with witnesses under 77(A)(iv).

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is, of course, a very specific, I would say, example of how contempt of court could be committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Your Honour put the question to me: Can he still be found guilty under 77(A)(iv) of interfering with witnesses if the witnesses weren't aware that their identities in fact had been disclosed. It's our position that -- that he can be, because the risk of repercussions to the witnesses who testified in the Blaskic case, even if the witnesses aren't aware of the publication, that there still might be repercussions against them in the future and they're unaware of their identity being disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The same would not be true for, I would say, the overall category of potential future witnesses. So then in this -- if you explain 77(A)(iv) in this way, then your case would be limited to the names of witnesses on the list whether aware or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But there's also the issue of interfering with other potential witnesses as a result of what he did. Other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that if I see my neighbour beating another neighbour that this might frighten me because the same could happen to me. That's the effect of the offence. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it might not be the offence itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out what, in your view, the offence is. Is the offence interference with all potential future witnesses and that under 77(A)(iv), or do you say he interfered with witnesses on the list because they even not being aware, they may have -- they may experience in the future intimidation, whatever, by persons who have seen that list, and this is very serious because it affects all potential witnesses for the future. That's the consequence of this offence. Is that your position? Because then it's not interference with future potential witnesses but with these witnesses, and then you explain, perhaps for sentencing purposes, how important it is that this should not happen. I'm just trying to find out exactly what your case is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We're saying that the accused can be found guilty under 77(A)(iv) with interfering with witnesses for two reasons, because of the interference on a personal level, and that may be as a consequence of the breach of 77(A)(ii), but we say it also rises to interference with witnesses under 77(A)(iv). So there's the first thing, it's a personal interference, but then there's also the interference with the administration of justice, because some of these witnesses aren't prepared to cooperate with the ICTY in the future or with national courts. So it's a two-pronged effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time when I asked you whether the witnesses should be aware, you said no, it's not necessary that they are aware because they, even if not aware, they could have to face the reactions by others who have seen that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that, of course, is a reasoning which could not apply to the general category of future potential witnesses because their name is not there. No one could go to them and say, "I know that you testified before the Tribunal and, therefore, never do that again." They are unidentified persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And still my question, therefore, is: Are you talking about the consequence of the interference with identified witnesses, that the reason why it should not be done is because it might keep others off from ever offering or accepting to testify before this Tribunal, or do you say, no 77(A)(iv), the offence there is committed in relation to all those unknown future unidentified potential witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Put your microphone off if you consult, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's our position that 77(A)(iv) captures both, and it's not inconsistent, the position that you just put. You can have interference with specific witnesses, but you can also have interference with potential witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would still fall under 77(A)(iv) and not just be covered by the heading of 77(A).

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. That can be covered by 77(A), interference with the administration of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but also covered by (A)(iv)?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both? Okay. That's at least a clear answer. Then, as I said before --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Moving on to the other matters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can respond to a couple of the matters that the Defence raised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- in relation to the Prosecution can make some stipulations, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what I tried to explore is what is agreed, although not giving it, as usual, in a list specifying exactly, but the areas, to see where there seems to be agreement between the parties and the areas where there seems to be dispute among the parties. If you want to say something about it, please proceed. If there's -- but I with like to avoid at this moment to start a debate on what is true and what is not true. I just wanted to explore more what we should focus on when hearing the case or for you when presenting the case. But if you'd like to make a few comments, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the Prosecution's position, the reason why we put "on or about the 7th of July, 2006," was taken from the HINA article, where the accused said himself that he -- on the 2nd of August, that he published the information three weeks ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I would say that's matter of evidence. It's clearly a matter of evidence. You put in the indictment "on or about the 7th." We see that that's a matter in dispute, so we'll hear in the evidence why you think it was on the 7th or --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are happy to stipulate that it was published on the web site. If the accused stipulates that he did, in fact, publish the witness list and the three articles on www.domagojmargetic.com web site, we can stipulate that it wasn't published -- that it was published after the 11th of July, 2006. That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's not an issue for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you do not insist on the 7th --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so we could focus the case on what the liability is of this accused if he published this on or after the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- certainly clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to the ownership, it's our view that ownership is irrelevant. We are prepared to stipulate, in order to narrow the issues, that Domagoj Margetic was not the registered owner of the web site, but we don't concede that at the time he did not have the capability to upload or download and/or pass information. But we do stipulate to the fact that at the time he published the witness list and the articles he wasn't the registered owner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we have to understand the indictment where it says his web site as being the web site --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The web site --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where he could put articles on and take them off. Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Or pass information to persons to put information on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On or from.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miljevic, we don't have to -- I think, to pay a lot of attention to possession or ownership of the web site since we now understand that it's not the position of the Prosecution that Mr. Margetic was the registered owner or the registered possessor of the web site, and that -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I can just add, the reason -- using the word "his," as Your Honour rightly pointed out, the Defence, in fact, on page 3 of the pre-trial brief that they filed yesterday -- the translation yesterday, talks about his web site, and it was simply talking about his web site because it's www.domagojmargetic.com. But, in fact, it can read "the web site."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now then talk about my street, and I'm not the owner of my street, I can tell you for sure. That issue seems to be clarified sufficiently as well. Any other matter, Ms. Sutherland, where --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, does the Chamber want to hear me in relation to the fact that the Defence say that the witness list was public between X date and Y date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I expect that the Defence will say -- that the Defence will bring evidence or will say something about the public character of the information during the period the 11th of July until the 22nd of August? Legal argument about it, we could leave that until after we are informed, because until now it is the Defence who says that it was public and we'll -- if the parties do not present any evidence on that, and if it is such a key for the Defence case, then the Chamber might even be interested in getting full information. But, of course, I expect the Defence to bring evidence. Yes, Mr. Miljevic. But if the parties could agree on that as well. If the parties are in agreement that on from a certain moment the list was in -- was a public document --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's the Prosecution's position that it's always been confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's always been confidential, and it's the position of the Defence that it was public. So, therefore, the parties agree that until the 7th it was protected material, and the Prosecution takes the position that also after the 11th, it still was protected material.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might be good to inform the Chamber about why the Prosecution takes that position since, most likely, this will be challenged by the Defence. So paying proper attention to that might be not a bad idea. Now, or -- well, if you can make any stipulations on the matter so we have at least a factual basis to proceed on, that would be a good idea as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. It's our position that the document was confidential, has always been confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. But we also noticed that on the 11th of July as we heard from Mr. Miljevic there may have happened something in the Jovic case. Whether or not this affects the confidentiality, perhaps the parties could agree on what happened without agreeing on the legal consequences of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document in question was admitted in that case on the 3rd of July, so we are at a loss to know what the relevance of the 11th of July is in any event to that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it tendered or was it admitted on the 3rd of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It was admitted pursuant to -- as I understand it, pursuant to a decision of the 3rd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Without at this moment making an issue out of the 3rd of July or the 11th of July, it was admitted as a -- is it the Prosecution's position, do you stipulate that it was admitted under seal or not under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's our position that it was admitted under seal and that it's the registry court records that have caused the confusion in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, if you would like to make any further stipulations at a later point you may always do that, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour is going to make a ruling or hear submissions from the Defence in relation to the Rule 89(C) motion that we filed to seek the Rule 65 ter exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have not heard the -- we have not heard yet the position of the Defence on that. It's the admission of -- of documentary material, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall avail myself of this particular opportunity to say something about the order of these proceedings. On the 31st of October of this year, a court order was issued with regard to the start of trial. Already then these deadlines could not have been met from 65 ter (E) or from 65 ter (F), because from the day the court order was issued, the Scheduling Order regarding this case, there were only 29 days available to this day. Therefore, six weeks, three weeks, and other time-limits envisaged in 65 ter (E) and 65 ter (F) could not have been met. I would like to say that the Scheduling Order was provided to the Croatian Ministry of Justice on the 16th of November. I received Ms. Del Ponte's submissions on the 24th of November. As for all the other material, on the 25th or the 28th of November. I think that now it would be a good opportunity if you were to draw on your authority from Rule 127 to change the time-limits, at least to ensure 126 bis; that is to say, the minimum requirement of 14 days. I would now like to ask the Trial Chamber, taking into account these facts, that from the day the Scheduling Order is issued regarding the start of trial the 65 ter deadlines could not have been met, and as for the trial -- for the brief issued, filed by the Prosecution seven days elapsed and for other material even less. I read all of this. There is quite a bit of scope for stipulations between the two parties as we could see through the proceedings today. However, my client knows nothing about that. I admit that if that is the point of Rule 89, then I do hereby recognise that I received from the OTP everything that they claim that they have submitted to me, and there are certain cover sheets that I saw in the Prosecution material. I would like to take this opportunity, now that I have the floor anyway, to say that the Prosecutor obviously stipulated the main thing with the Defence; namely, she said that on the 2nd of August, my client said to his interview in HINA that he published the said article three weeks before that. We know that July has 31 days. Then at any rate, there are two days in August. So these are the three weeks, which would make it the 12th of July, and that is after the 11th of July. Now, why -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are evidently matters not to be discussed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I would like to know is, first of all, you said that the time-limits were not kept, that -- well, let's not at this moment discuss whether this was implicitly changed by a Scheduling Order, and let's also not discuss at this very moment, unless you feel that there is need to do so, whether in a contempt case all the usual time-limits would apply automatically. When you said that -- when you explained to us when you received material and that there's one day missing of the 30-day period, you were talking about the two-week period, does this prevent you from proceeding? Do you say, "This is a problem which has consequences for me, for my ability to defend the case today," or would we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for this material, I received all of it and I confirmed that. I even managed to read all of it, although I received some of this material only the day before yesterday, which can be proven. However, my client has no knowledge of this. I think that indeed for the sake of the quality of the defence it would be necessary to change some of the time-limits, and that the Defence should state its positions regarding what the Prosecution said as early as possible but, say, within 14 days or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask the Prosecution to what extent all the material is still necessary in view of large agreement on facts today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can go through the material, the evidence in the break and let Your Honours know exactly what we -- documents we still seek to have admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But they would certainly be all of the statements or admissions by the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that that material is -- the accused is aware of. I mean, documents he signed himself, he submitted, for example. I would not easily accept that he would have to study them first before taking a position in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Defence has been in possession of the supporting material since the 13th of October, and all of the Rule 65 ter material which was disclosed on the 16th of November when we filed our pre-trial brief. What the Defence is now saying they only received on the 25th was the statement, the witness statements, and we don't seek to have those statements admitted because we're leading that evidence from the witnesses, and that was disclosed on the 25th of November pursuant to the Judges' -- the Trial Chamber's order. So as soon as we got the order we disclosed it. But all the other material, which is relevant to the 89(C) motion, was disclosed on the 13th of October to the accused himself, because -- and then the Rule 65 ter stuff on the 16th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's time for a break. The Chamber would like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one moment. Before the break, the issue of Mr. Osorio's evidence, are we able to get that sorted before the break so that we can determine whether in fact his memorandum is going to be admitted pursuant to the Defence agreement via the letter that we got yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, there was a -- now, I have to refer to what happened yesterday during an informal meeting I had with the parties. Unfortunately, it could not be a formal meeting since Defence counsel arrived only relatively late yesterday, and we were talking about practicalities for today's trial. One of the issues raised there was an exchange of correspondence between the Prosecution and Defence, the question being whether Mr. Osorio should be called as a witness or whether admission of a statement given by him would be acceptable for the Defence. The Prosecution, as far as I understood yesterday, received a letter from Mr. Miljevic stating that there was no need to call Mr. Osorio as a witness. Mr. Miljevic, does that include that you accept that the written statement of Mr. Osorio would be admitted into evidence and that there's no need to cross-examine Mr. Osorio on that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's what I said informally yesterday, and I confirm it today, and I make things easier by virtue of that fact. If that pertains to the document dated the 14th of September, 2006, and that is the only document that I found that could have anything to do with Mr. Osorio, as I wrote in my filing yesterday, I'm absolutely not opposed to having that particular submission in evidence and not to have Mr. Osorio called to testify. However, if it's something else in addition to that, then I don't know. That's the only document that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will verify this with Ms. Sutherland. Is it the 14th of September?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the 11th of August, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break anyhow, and the parties are invited not only to review their own positions in relation to -- in relation to what evidence still needs to be presented, but also to briefly discuss, perhaps have an exchange on material, written material, by Mr. Osorio. So there seems to be some conclusion about whether there's only 14th of September material or also 11th of August, I think it was. So would you please clarify that during the break. We will then give a ruling after having been informed by the parties. Perhaps for those reasons we should take a little bit longer break, half an hour. We adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the parties whether the Osorio matter has been discussed and resolved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has. The Defence have agreed that Exhibit 21 on the Rule 65 ter list can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: They have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have the habit to -- to accept what one of the parties says unless the other clearly disagrees. So if Ms. Sutherland says that there's an agreement, then I take it there is. That being clarified, then, could you please -- Ms. Sutherland, could you -- could you please tell us what remains from the 89(C) motion. The advantage of having this material in evidence is that we have an overall agreement on most of the facts, I would say, apart from a few. Of course in these documents, which are mainly documents of a rather objective nature, at least many of them, would enable the Chamber to use them in preparing a judgement, either in favour of the Prosecution or perhaps the same documents in favour of the Defence. When I say "objective documents," it is, for example, if we have the text of what was exactly published, if there's no disagreement about publication of a list or the text of an article, that if this reflects this article it would be good to have in evidence because we did not go into that much detail when I explored what the issues in dispute were. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps if we can start with Table A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Table A.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if the Defence has that in front of them, too, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I'm looking at the motion. You're looking at the table at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The table's attached to -- Tables A to D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Table A. Yes. Perhaps you first tell us what you do not need anymore, and then -- or I don't know whether you discussed it already with Mr. Miljevic, and then we'll hear from Mr. Miljevic what his position is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. -- The Defence were kind enough to also agree to Rule 65 ter Exhibit 17 being admitted with no objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is on --

utterances.text: If you briefly --

utterances.text: -- Table D.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Yes, this is 17. That's the Osorio 14th of September, is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But if we go back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We go back to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- Table A we obviously need Exhibit 1, which is the witness list that was published.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Miljevic, to have it admitted not having been introduced by any witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no objections whatsoever, either in reference to Exhibit number 1 or the one under 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 1 and 17, therefore, can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in the absence of any objection the Chamber will admit -- and I'm now using the number, 65 ter number 1 and 17. Then what else would you need?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then 4 is admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

I believe [indiscernible] gives a bit of the text. Any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 10, printout of the web site, 15th of July, 2006, authored by Domagoj Margetic, and then: "Who were The Hague Prosecution's protected witnesses?" That's the quote with a question mark. Any objection against that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The description of the document, the article actually comes from Domagoj Margetic's web site. That's the -- the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, we have it in both. We have it from both web sites, but Exhibit number 10 comes from his web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Number 11 is a printout of a web site, also 15th of July --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, that's also from Margetic's web site, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that here again the source, the www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com is wrong and should be the Domagoj Margetic web site as cited before.

utterances.text: Number 12, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: X.

utterances.text: Why was X a protected witness in The Hague. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Number 12 is the Google cache report for web site www.011385.com re the Margetic article "List of secret witnesses" which in fact has just been admitted as Exhibit 6, but this exhibit gives the full text in B/C/S, because in Exhibit 6 the B/C/S version has been cut off down one side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it also shows that it was on this web site www.011385.com. So we would seek to have that admitted to show the -- the different web sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't say anything about ownership or possession. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Miljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12 is the Google cache report for web site www.011385.com is admitted into evidence. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Exhibit number 13 the print without of the web site www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com showing the -- the links -- the two articles which are now Exhibits 10 and 11. So we seek to have that document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's more of an administrative nature. Any objections, Mr. Miljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 18 the Vecernji List newspaper article dated the 4th of August is admitted into evidence. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Exhibit number 25 is Domagoj Margetic's official statement dated the 12th of September, 2006, published on the web site www.croatianworldwideassociation.com. We seek to have that admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection, Mr. Miljevic? You're nodding yes, but may --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Domagoj Margetic official statement dated the 12th of September as published on the web site just referred to by Ms. Sutherland is admitted into evidence. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Turning now to Table D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: We've discussed Exhibit 17.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dated the 20th of August, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miljevic, any objection against that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have dealt with all of them, Ms. Sutherland, if I'm not mistaken, or -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave I would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have now dealt with all the exhibits on the OTP's list. However, in the documents which were submitted to me by the OTP, we also have the press conference of this Tribunal of the 23rd of August, 2006. After that, we have a document list of cases and decisions rendered by this Tribunal in the different cases, and on that list under the date 22nd of August we have Blaskic and the Kordic and Cerkez contempt, and the decision -- this is the exhibit which I was given by the OTP, and I should like that document to also be admitted into the file because it was submitted by them to me. Apart from that, on the list of exhibits which have -- with which we have just dealt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, if I may just interfere. If documents are disclosed by the Prosecution to you and if they're not tendered into evidence, I don't know whether at any further stage the Prosecution will seek admission of these documents, if it has not sought admission of these documents, it's entirely up to you while presenting the Defence case whether or not you want to present these documents, fortunately already they're in two languages, to be admitted into evidence, but I don't think that we should do that before even the Prosecution had started presenting its case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't disclosed this material to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You haven't disclosed --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we will see that. But if there are any documents -- that was one of the issues we discussed yesterday evening on a very practical level whether the Defence would seek any documentary evidence to be admitted. It -- of course then should be presented in at least one of the official languages of this court. Let's keep it to that. You'll have an opportunity later to present whatever evidence the Defence would like to present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, flexible as always, changes the order a little bit. We'd like now to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, the first witness the Prosecution would like to call is that a protected witness or is that an unprotected witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution now calls Mirjana Oklobdzija, and Mr. Cannata will put the questions pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are presenting this evidence under Rule 92 ter. Mr. Miljevic, you are aware of what Rule 92 ter means in this respect. That is, that the witness will not be examined but that the written statement will be admitted into evidence, that the witness is present in court and that you have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness. The first witness being, Ms. Sutherland, you said Ms. Mirjana Oklobdzija. Yes. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Given the admission by the Defence that Mr. Osorio's memorandum of the 11th of August, 2006, will be admitted with no objection, we will not be calling him. Can the registrar or the usher get a message to the witnesses MC1 and MC2 that they can return to -- to the hotel and that the office -- someone from the Office of the Prosecutor will be speaking with them as soon as this -- we finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because I can imagine that it needs some explanation for the witnesses why they were not called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I take it you will take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. I may have some difficulties in pronouncing your name properly. Perhaps you could give us your name, although it's usually the first question put by the calling party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your name is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirjana Oklobdzija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oklobdzija. Yes, I'll try to do my best. Before you give evidence in this court, and you are called as a witness by the Prosecution, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to give a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Ms. Oklobdzija. Ms. Sutherland, I take it that the witness is aware of the procedure under Rule 92 ter or -- that's you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The witness is a research officer with the leadership research team of the Office of the Prosecutor. The witness's responsibilities at the Tribunal include analysis of public documents in order to detect any information concerning Tribunal's past, current, or pending cases and search for relevant data. As part of her duties, on 26th July, 2006, the witness checked the web site www.domagojmargetic.com and noticed there a publication entitled "Exclusive: List of confidential witnesses in The Hague given to me by an assistant of Carla Del Ponte." Attached to the above-mentioned article the witness found on the same web site the path, which is www.domagojmargetic.com/media/POPISTAJNIHSVJEDOKA.pdf, which led to a separate document entitled POPISTAJNIHSVJEDOKA, which is to be translated as "list of secret witnesses." The witness opened this document and observed that it appeared to be a list of the names of witnesses in the Blaskic case explicitly marked as confidential. The list was accessible via the aforementioned web page path. The witness informed the OTP staff working in the Blaskic review case about the article and the attached list and handed over printouts of the B/C/S version of the article as well as the list of witnesses published on the web site. And that completes the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, to call it a summary it's almost a complete reading of it. Next time you're invited to make it a summary, because one of the reasons, it's just to inform the public because the document as such is known to the parties. For the Defence now to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: By your leave, I would just ask one question -- a couple of questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Because it goes without saying that the Prosecution seek to tender the Exhibit 7 of the Prosecution Rule 65 ter exhibit list, which is the witness statement into exhibit. That is the preliminary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness statement dated the 29th of August, 2006. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And before we do that, we actually, for the record, would like to comply with prescription of Rule 92 ter by asking the witness to authenticate the witness [sic]. So by your leave, I would like to ask a few questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Please state your full name and for the record spell it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: My full name is Mirjana Oklobdzija.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 29th of August, 2006?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review this statement during our proofing session on the 28th of November, 2006?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Is this statement true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you attest that the statement accurately reflects your declaration and what you would say if you were asked the same questions again today?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, as anticipated before, I seek to tender the -- into evidence Exhibit 7 of the Prosecution Rule 65 ter exhibit list, which is the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Miljevic, against submission of the witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I have copies for --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you will have an opportunity to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Once again, by your leave, Your Honour, I will just put two questions for the sake of clarification and then I will be done with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I please ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit 1 of the Prosecution Rule 65 exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes, that is the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Could you expand on this answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the list which was -- back to -- which was attached to the article which I found on 26th of July on the web page www.domagojmargetic.com.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I move on to Exhibit 6, with the kind assistance of the usher. Would you please show the witness Exhibit 6 of the Prosecution 65 exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yeah. This document is translation of the original article which I found on the 26th of July on the web page in B/C/S, the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to turn to the original article in B/C/S, which is the document --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the original article.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: In B/C/S, Exhibit 6.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now I ask you again the question: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, what document is this?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: This is -- shall I read the title in --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: As you --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Croat? [Interpretation] "Exclusive: List of confidential Hague witnesses given to me by Carla Del Ponte's assistant."

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. I saw it on the 26th [Realtime transcript read in error "267th"] of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: On the web page www.domagojmargetic.com.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no further questions. I think both the documents are already admitted into evidence under Rule 89(C), so, therefore, we don't have to take any further decisions on that it. Mr. Miljevic, you have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness. Witness -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I notice the date, it's supposed to be 26th of July but it says "267th" of July. We may never know if it was 26th or 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's now on the record. That saves us at least listening to a lot of tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was the 26th of July. Perhaps for the witness: You said it was the 26th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 26th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Miljevic, you may cross-examine the witness. Witness, Mr. Miljevic is Defence counsel for Mr. Margetic. Mr. Miljevic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, as far as I understood, at your workplace in the OTP of the International Tribunal, you examine documentation and you analyse documents referring to cases before the Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Before the 26th of July, 2006, did you have occasion to examine what referred to the internet page of Domagoj Margetic?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: [In English] I was looking at that web page on a regular basis, which doesn't mean daily but regular, because Mr. Margetic was accused before this Tribunal before. But it wasn't on a daily basis. Yes, from time to time I was looking at that web page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: That is exactly why I asked. Can you be more specific? When did you start to regularly monitor his web page?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
utterances.text: Several months before that, when Mr. Margetic had problems with this Tribunal on account of his first disclosure, publication of the testimonies of a protected witness in the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: You said that this was not a daily thing but a regular matter. Can you say something in between? What would "regularly" imply and not on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA OKLOBDZIJA
