utterances.text: Well, at a time when someone is already before a tribunal or is scheduled to appear before a tribunal, then it can be also on a daily basis. In the case of Mr. Margetic, who no longer was indicted by our Tribunal, that was no longer on a regular basis because we thought that that problem had been overcome. However, as it was still relatively recent, I looked at it every couple of weeks or 10 days; namely, examined his web page on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miljevic. Is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: No. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to thank you very much for coming, Ms. Oklobdzija.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oklobdzija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Oklobdzija. I'm learning, slowly. I'd like to thank you very much for coming in to answer questions of the parties. I first have to verify whether the Bench has any further questions. I assumed we would not have, but now that's verified as well. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your next witness, Ms. Sutherland, would be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Carry Spork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher may not be aware that ... A summary would really do. The purpose of it is that the public is at least aware when listening to the cross-examination of the witness what is the core of the statement that is at that moment in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution intends calling Mr. Spork viva voce as set out in the Rule 65 ter witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And time you would need approximately would be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Spork -- at least I take it you are Mr. Spork. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but truth. The text is now handed out now by Madam Usher, may invite you to make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you please be seated. You'll first be examined by Ms. Sutherland, counsel of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Spork, you were born in Holland on the 6th of January, 1958?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: After completing secondary school, you joined the Dutch military?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in 1979, you joined the Dutch police and until 1995 worked as an investigator on serious crimes, including murders, narcotics, and a kidnapping case?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: And that's correct too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, should we not first, before we know when he's born, know who is he?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Spork, can you state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: My name is Carry Spork.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In March 1996, you were seconded by the Dutch government to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, becoming a UN staff member in 1998?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Besides a six-month leave of absence to work in the UN Office of Internal Oversight in the Congo from October 2005 until April 2006, from 1996 until the present you have been investigating crimes committed in the Herceg-Bosna area of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina and Herceg-Bosna both.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: As part of your duties, you were also tasked to investigate matters pertaining to the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What and when were you tasked to do in this regard?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Initially I was tasked to look at the internet site of Mr. Domagoj Margetic, which was known as www.domagojmargetic.com, and the purpose of that was to establish the web host of that internet site in order to see what possibilities there were to close down the internet site.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What else were you tasked to do in relation to the -- the web hosts?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Besides the web hosts, I was looking on the web page to see what kind of information was revealed on the web site and in addition if there were any linkages to the web site from other web sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court which web sites you viewed?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I initially reviewed the Domagoj Margetic web site. Then via Google I searched for leads to other web sites and I ended up with three additional web sites which had a direct linkage to the Domagoj Margetic web site. The first one was www.011385.com. The second web site was www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com. And the third web site was www.hrvatska-hrvatom.com. And -- and these three -- the last three web sites that are mentioned all had a direct linkage to the Domagoj Margetic web site.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you open any documents on -- any documents on these web sites?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: The first document I opened was a list of witnesses that was revealed on the Domagoj Margetic web site, and once I went to the other web sites it was possible via these web sites to get direct linkage to the Domagoj Margetic web site on which you could see these lists, and in addition on www.011385.com, as well as www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com I found two articles that also had a linkage to the Domagoj Margetic web sites but besides that they contained a text, actually some kind of a publication, that was done by Mr. Domagoj Margetic. That's how it looked at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes. This is the documents that I saw on the Domagoj Margetic web site and which I actually printed a copy of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the date that you saw it on that web site?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: On the 31st of July, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. This is one of the articles I was referring to which was published on the two web sites I mentioned before. So the 011385 as well as the www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com web site. To make it easy let's call it Lijepa web site. And in addition, there was a heading -- this article had a heading on the initial web page, web site, and you could -- there was a reference that said "text" and if you would double-click on text the whole publication would be -- you would be able to read the whole publication. In addition, it made a reference, and as I -- as far as I remember it said 15th of July, 2006, Domagoj Margetic, and via that you could double-click on that web site, get back to the original web site, which was Domagoj Margetic, where you could also find this article.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: This is the -- the second article that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to -- we have not earlier dealt with whether or not material was admitted under seal or not. Certainly 13 would be something to be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please review your list of documents whether there's any of the other documents before coming into the public record whether they need to be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might well be that many of them are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the -- in the table to Rule 65 ter list there was a final column saying confidential or not confidential, and we ticked -- there was either yes or no there, but we will be very clear in what we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My request is that admission should be only in accordance with what you indicated there. Would there be any problem with that, Mr. Miljevic, since we are now looking at some of these documents? All confidential -- all documents qualified as confidential by the Prosecution to be admitted under seal not as public documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: As far as the interpreter could hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the decisions on admission are all in accordance with the confidentiality note in the 65 ter list. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we will double-check the list to make sure that there are no other documents which are required to be put under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, if described as confidential, that means admission under seal. Yes. Please proceed. I noticed that, to some extent, we are already a bit repetitious, also in view of the stipulations made today by the parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Spork, can you look at the B/C/S version of Exhibit 13.

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do we see there what you were referring to earlier in your evidence about the 15th of July, 2006?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct. It's almost -- it's the third paragraph, which says, "15th Srpnja 06 Domagoj Margetic," and then the text, and then the other paragraph, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you subsequently check these web sites again; if, so, what did you observe?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I checked the web site again on the 4th of August, 2006, and I saw on both web sites that these articles were still there. And I could open the articles and read the articles -- still read the articles. But when I tried to open -- to go to the Domagoj Margetic web site, the hyperlink -- it appeared that the web host had temporarily, or at least closed down the web page, so I could not open that any more from these two -- from this -- these two web sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the two web sites you're referring to, so that the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's www.011385.com and www.lijepanasadomovinahrvatska.com.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I turn now to another topic. Did you have contact any of the witnesses whose identities had been disclosed by the accused; and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I had contact with these witnesses twice, at least three of the witnesses twice; the first time, on the 8th of September, 2006, and the second time, on the 19th and 20th of September, 2006, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you take any statements from these witness?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: During my first contact on the 8th of September, I discussed with them their feelings, about how they will felt that their names had been disclosed or published. And then on the 19th and 20th of September, 2006, I met the people in person and I took statements from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you identify these witnesses by referring to their pseudonyms?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: You mean the current pseudonyms or the pseudonyms before?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The pseudonyms they've been given in this case.

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's MC1, MC2, and MC3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just interrupt your questioning. I just want to find out from Mr. Spork, you're saying that on the 19th and 20th, you met them in person. Had you not met them in person on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 8th I called them in order to see how they felt, and since I was on a mission in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 19th of September, it was decided that I would meet them in person and take a statement from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the reason why you took the statements from them at that time, on the 19th and 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Initially the statement was taken from them by one of my colleagues on, I think, the 15th of November, and after having received the statement, it was decided that we might have to expand or clarify certain points that were given in the earlier statement. And that was the reason why I met them, to see if they would be willing to expand and clarify certain issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In respect to witnesses MC1 and MC2, were they willing to testify in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: They were willing to testify under certain conditions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what conditions were those?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: The first condition would be that they would be granted protective measures as they had been granted in their previous testimony in the Blaskic trial. But, in addition, they didn't want the accused in this proceeding to know their actual names.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if that protective measure wasn't granted by the Trial Chamber, were they still willing to testify?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: No. They made it very clear that only under these conditions they would be willing to testify. If their names would be revealed to the accused in this case, they would not testify, in no way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, you may cross-examine the witness. Mr. Miljevic is counsel for the Defence, just for your information, Mr. Spork.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Spork, when you established what you described just now on the 31st of July, 2006, did you write a document about that, a statement?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I wrote an affidavit on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber on what date this was?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That must be the day after that, so it must be the beginning of September. Maybe -- I'm not completely sure, but the first week of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're confusing us. You're confusing us a bit, Mr. Spork. The question was about when you established, that you described just now, on the 31st of July, and then you say a couple of days later and you're talking about the beginning of September. Could you clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I did the investigation on the internet site and I gathered all the information I needed in order to be able to write the affidavit. I printed the pages, I printed the other documents, and then I wrote an affidavit based on the outcome of that initial investigation that I started on the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That certainly clarifies what is a couple of days after. So I take it you started your investigation the 31st of July. It then took you quite some time to gather documents, to put everything together, and that you then wrote an affidavit relatively -- well, a couple of weeks after that. Is that the correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Am I reaching the proper conclusion if I say that in August you did not write any statement or affidavit?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I -- I have to say I'm not sure anymore. It could be August, it could be beginning the September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you say something a lot simpler, a lot easier? How many affidavits or statements did you write in respect of what you established on the 31st of July?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I wrote at least four affidavits. I took one statement of a colleague from the leadership research team and in addition I took three statements of persons whose name had been revealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm interested in -- only in what you established on the 31st of July when you found the list of witnesses. In respect of that, did you make any other statements or affidavits?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: You mean about the 31st of July, 2006? The initial affidavit dealt with what was found on the internet, the documentation that was found on the internet, the publications that were made on the different internet sites. It also included documentation regarding the web host, and then in addition I wrote additional affidavits that became apparent -- regarding information that became apparent after the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely why I'm asking you this. Are all your statements about that, that is to say what you saw on the 31st of July, 2006? Are all of your statements the same or are they different?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: All these statements are different because it's -- it's a follow-up and one leads to another. One part -- one -- one part of the investigation leads to another which made it necessary to write an additional affidavit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this published list that you recognised just now? Was it only a confidential list or was there a public list involved as well?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I don't know to what extent the public list was public. I do, however, recollect that the first list -- it were actually three similar lists. The first list -- all three lists were in French. The first list said "Confidential," and it had a capital letter C in front of "confidential" with two stars on the side. The second document similar to the first one said also "confidential," and then behind that "not to be distributed." And the third list had no markings on it. But all three lists were the same lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the term Annex A, and did you attach anything from this annex to your affidavits that had to do with what you had established on the 31st of July?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: You mean the Annex A to my affidavit, to my first affidavit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: As I said, I printed the witness lists and I attached them as an Annex A to my affidavit. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Now, finally, the most important question. Did you remember later on that this first affidavit you gave in relation to Annex A was not correct, and then you made yet another affidavit, another statement on the 20th of September specifically?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I do, sir. Later on when I check the material, I found out that even though all the papers had been printed and attached to the affidavit I found out that two pages were missing, and I wrote an affidavit on that and then attached these two missing pages to the second affidavit. However, I would like to stress that when I wrote my first affidavit and attached the annexes that was a complete set, and I mean all three similar lists were attached as an Annex A. And only when after checking and when I noticed that these two pages were missing I discussed this with my superior and we decided I should write an additional affidavit and explain what I noticed and then attach these -- the lists again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: And the last question: Does that mean that your first affidavit was wrong or untruthful in respect of Annex A?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: No, definitely not, because as I told you I printed all the three sets of papers and I attached them as Annex A. How two pages of this annex got missing I don't know, but once we noticed they were not included in the bundle, that's when we decided to write an additional affidavit and attach them again. But no, no. It was not untruthful, and it was not wrong either. I mean, the initial affidavit included all pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: But the annex did not have those two, right?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Initially it had, but apparently somewhere during processing two pages got missing or lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, we have to have a break very, very soon. How much time would you still need? If it would be one minute or half a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I finished. I finished. I don't even need a minute. This was my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Miljevic. Any need to re-examine the witness? It's only relevant for what I'm going to tell the witness now, because we would have to do it anyhow after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I just have one small area --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to have a break now because otherwise -- so we'll have to do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to address the Court, you can do that through counsel. So during the -- if that would lead to any additional question, we'll give an opportunity to that after the break, Mr. Margetic, we'll hear from the counsel. We'll have a break until five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like, first of all, the witness to be escorted into the courtroom again and to inquire with the parties on their availability after today. Mr. Miljevic, would you be available tomorrow? When are you leaving, Mr. Miljevic? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in several contacts with the administration of this Tribunal, I was told that it would be only one day, whereas I have some engagements in Zagreb tomorrow that cannot be postponed at all, at several hearings, and a very important hearing in Zadar. But far more important than that is the fact that at 3.00 in the afternoon I am going to be an examiner at the bar examination in the Ministry of Justice of Croatia, and that is where the programme cannot be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what time do you have to leave The Hague, Mr. Miljevic, because that was the core of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime today, late in the afternoon. I was told verbally that this would go on until 2.00 today, possibly until --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear to me. It's just for my information. Then the Prosecution asked to put one or more questions to the witness in re-examination. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness be shown Exhibit 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Spork, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes ma'am. This is my first affidavit which I wrote on the 4th of August, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And attached to that affidavit as Annex A?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is the witness list?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: It is, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see the three versions of the witness list there attached?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: I have only two versions, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And which versions are they?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: These were the two versions with the markings on it. The first one with C -- with a star, "Confidential," which is -- and the send one with "Confidential not distribute."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the one with star "confidential" consists of how many pages?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: It consists of three pages and it's missing the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the one marked "confidential do not distribute" consists of how many pages?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: It consists of four pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the public version is not annexed?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Not -- not in this folder, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one additional question in relation to this? You say these were annexes to your first affidavit, which is dated the 4th of August. Now, I see some handwriting on the top of the "confidential not to distribute" copy, and it says "copied from," and then I can't read it, "files," and then a date is attached which the month very much appears to be a 9. Could you comment on that, Mr. Spork?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only see -- see the same things as you do, Your Honour. It says 30, 9, 1995, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1995, yes. Any clue as to what that means, this 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I don't, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any idea on who put this date on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you look at Exhibit number 9, please. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. This is a follow-up on my first affidavit regarding the missing of the first page of the first set of documents and the fact that the public list was not contained in my Annex A.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the date that you became aware of that was?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: The 13th of October. I wrote the affidavit on the 13th of October, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you became aware of it -- of the pages missing on the 20th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you were questioned earlier by the Defence in relation to Annex A, you said that two pages were missing from the document, but do you -- do you still stick by that answer, or from what you've just told us it seems to be different?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am. It's my mistake. I meant for the first -- the first document, which consists of the C confidential the last page is missing and the whole public list was missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown Exhibit 14, please. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. This is the affidavit I wrote after I contacted the three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the date of the contact with the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: CARRY SPORK
utterances.text: That date was the 8th of September, and I wrote the affidavit the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, these affidavits are not in evidence yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they need to be assigned a number at least. So we're talking about three affidavits now, and they should be under seal anyhow. These are the affidavits found on the 65 ter list under 8 -- 9 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and 14, all being affidavits. The first one - let me just have a look - I think it's the 4th of August. The second one -- or am I making a mistake now. No. I think the first one the 4th of August, the second one dated the 13th of October, 2006, and the third one, 14, is the 8th of September, 2006. All three 2006. Yes. Any objection, Mr. Miljevic, to the admission of these documents in evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections. That's exactly what I asked the witness about, because it's obvious that there are at least three statements or affidavits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but they were not in evidence yet. Admitted -- yes. These are admitted into evidence. Judge Moloto has a question for you, Mr. Spork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Spork. In your evidence you indicated that after discovering this web site on the 31st of July you wrote an affidavit first you said a few days later but then you said in September. I see the first affidavit that you referred to here is dated the 4th of August. Is there any explanation you can give for that, the 4th of August and September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That was my mistake. As I initially said, I was looking at the internet site and I was printing off all the documentation that I could find there in order to avoid that if the web site would be closed I would not be able to print it anymore, and as I initially said maybe a couple of days later, maybe a week later, I wrote my first affidavit and I made a mistake when I said afterwards that it could be maybe the end of August, because it was the 4th of August. This was definitely my first affidavit that I wrote when I started the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miljevic, I take it there are no -- there's further need to examine the witness? Then, Mr. Spork, this concludes your --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes your testimony in this court. I thank you very much for coming, although it was not very far, perhaps, but thank you very much, and madam usher will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness to be called by the Prosecution will be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Witness MC3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is a protected witness, and the protective measures are?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Court granted this witness protective measures for him to testify with a pseudonym, image, and voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we need a break to have the voice distortion in place. The Chamber would very much like to -- of course we should have done this before during the last break. I'm not fully aware of all the technicalities. What's the minimum time we -- the technicians would need, because we're really trying hard to see whether we can conclude the case today, but of course Defence still has to present its case. What's the minimum time?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be done between 3 and 5 minutes. We can even go into closed session. The technician will get and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the witness can be brought in at that point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not fully understand. We would then go into closed session, and then meanwhile the system would be adjusted and then later on we would -- yes. But then a small part of the testimony of the witness could not be seen, although this very blurry picture, nothing at all. Would that be any problem for you, Mr. Miljevic, if we would start in closed session and immediately move to -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand it, the audio booth needs to have a break or to go into closed session so that they can do the voice distortion. And so at that point the witness could be brought in, and then once the voice distortion is set up we can start his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we just wait here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't even go into closed session. We adjourn, as a matter of fact, we adjourn for the time needed to adjust for the voice distortion, and we'll resume then and perhaps even stay in the courtroom until that's done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll adjourn for a couple of minutes, the time needed for the adjustment of the voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume the hearing. Witness MC3, because that's -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness MC3, first of all, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I call you by this name because we will not use your real name. We'll use a pseudonym. Apart from that, your voice could not be directly heard by the outside world, and your face also is scrambled on our screens so that no one outside of this courtroom could see your face. Before you give evidence in this Tribunal, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by Ms. Sutherland, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Sutherland, I take it that we first go to the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness MC3, the Trial Chamber has granted you permission to testify today with a pseudonym, image, and voice distortion. Could you have a look at that piece of paper, and without mentioning your name can you confirm whether that's your name and your date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give your answer by saying something, because for our interpreters and for the audio record, it's important that we hear you say yes or no. Is it -- I take it from your nodding that you confirm that you found your name and date of birth on this piece of paper. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Madam Registrar, that pseudonym sheet will need a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit number 26. It will be under seal, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, and is admitted into evidence under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, you were recently informed by the Tribunal's victims and witness section that your identity had been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court your initial reaction to being advised of this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I can tell you it was difficult. It was exhausting. I still feel the consequences to this day in the sense of my security and what has been done to us witnesses, because when we came to take the stand here, we came because we believed all our rights would be guaranteed, and these rights have all been taken away from us. Now I'm suffering heavy traumas. I'm in severe pain.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can just pause you there. We will go into more -- which is, if you can just pause there. We will go into more detail in a moment in relation to that. But first when you spoke to Investigator Spork in early September 2006, what did you tell him at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I told him that I would come to testify in The Hague, and I have come, and I actually came, and I gave a statement as a protected witness under a protected name. And you see after that now that appeared in the papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, if I can just pause you there for a moment. When Mr. Spork initially spoke to you, were you initially reluctant to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to this case. When Mr. Spork spoke to you in September, you were willing -- you were initially reluctant to testify, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you that I hesitated because security is no longer guaranteed us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Spork contacted you again in November, and you agreed to meet with OTP investigators, and you subsequently provided two statements to investigators on the 15th and the 20th of November, 2006. You had an opportunity yesterday to review the B/C/S translations of those statements. Is there anything you wish to clarify in relation to either of those statements before we continue with your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: When I arrived, I gave the statement to the effect that I would come and take this witness stand here before this Tribunal, and I have come. And there you have it. I'm present right now to testify, to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just pause there, Witness. So have you suffered any physical consequences as a result?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: When they informed us, first they called us on the mobile phone, and they told us that we were uncovered as witnesses, that we had been revealed on the internet and in the papers, and that really -- I took it very hard, and I still feel the consequences to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court the consequences that you now suffer as a result of your name being disclosed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you first and foremost I'm no longer secure. Secondly, I have constant pains. I'm on medication at all times. And that's about it. I'm not feeling well. I am undergoing treatment. I have check-ups regularly. And I can't sleep simply. I experienced a severe stress then because my security was endangered. And at the same time, this affected my condition. I fell ill.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that you are currently undergoing treatment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that you were currently undergoing treatment. What sort of treatment is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Well, every month I go to see the doctor, a specialist. That's one. And secondly, I'm under constant control on his part. He -- he gives me all sorts of medicaments which will help me walk easier and to ease my condition, because I'm always fearful of the consequences that I can have as a witness here, namely after having been uncovered as a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is the treatment psychiatric treatment? Is the treatment you're currently undergoing under a psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: A psychiatrist, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When did you first start attending the psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I started seeing one when I found out about this matter. And I am still seeing him today, and I am still undergoing treatment, and I'm taking medicaments which is also hard for me because they are very expensive, the drugs which I have to take, and I really don't know who is going to keep me in those medicines, because when I came here the first time, to take the witness stand for the first time, I was told that we would be protected as witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, is this a copy of the document you gave me yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes. This is my documentation from the last time I went for a check-up, my last check-up. Here -- the drugs are in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, if it is under seal -- I do understand that we are using the MC3 pseudonym, but why could the Chamber at this moment not see the unredacted document? So that we, for example, could identify this witness as the person to whom this document relates?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, it could be anyone. You put MC3 on it and then it would be valid always, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I fully understand, Your Honour. We will have the original brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's tendered, and the original, if we then accept it under seal, I mean, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, do you have this document on your person? Could you please produce it and show it to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I do have it on my person. Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has verified that the name on the original is the same name as we find on the pseudonym sheet. At least the year of birth is the same. Does the Defence insist on having the original in evidence, or could we proceed on the basis, having established it, to return the document to the witness and to have the redacted statement in evidence? Or would you want to verify yourself, Mr. Miljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not need to verify it. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the redacted version will be admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 27. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, is it the fact that you commenced seeing a psychiatrist shortly after the events that happened to you which caused you to be a witness initially in the Blaskic case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes. That is why. It is from that time. And I came as a witness, and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then at some point with your psychiatric treatment did you have a break for some period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes, I had a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you were still under the medication that had been prescribed by the psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Now I am on those medicaments because my condition has worsened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you heard about the disclosure of your identity, you commenced seeing the psychiatrist again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know whether you want me to read the clinical examination into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a very short passage. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "After specific re-traumatisation, visible deterioration in condition." And does the Court want the medication on the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The document will be in evidence, so it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, are you willing to cooperate with the ICTY in the future?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I am willing if -- if what I have suffered is rectified because I came to see -- to be before this Tribunal, but before my case is resolved I am not willing to come because I want what has been inflicted on me to be made good. I want to be paid compensation. I am constantly on medicines. I'm unable to bear that. I want the accused to compensate for the damage which has been inflicted on me and which I am suffering today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, are you willing to cooperate with a national court if you were asked to testify in any cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I'm not willing, because -- because I have been humiliated here, and then nobody is guaranteeing my security. My security is very endangered where I live.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that completes my examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Mr. Miljevic, you have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness. Witness MC3, you'll now be examined by Mr. Miljevic, who is counsel for the Defence. Mr. Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, I'm not going to ask you much, just a couple of things. Can you tell the Honourable Bench when it was that you learned that this list was published and that your name was on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: It was in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? When in August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact day. I know that it was August. And as for the day, I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Was it in the first or in the second half of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I believe it was in the first half, but I'm not sure again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Tribunal from whom and how you learned about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I learned about it from the OTP in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: In which way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: They called me. They informed me. They told me that unfortunately we had been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: And when did you give a first statement about that and to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I gave it -- I cannot remember. I cannot remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps just a month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: They informed me about everything by telephone. They called me. I gave a statement 10 days ago for the Tribunal, but they informed me by phone. So we had a telephone conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you learned that your name had been published? When was it that you saw a psychiatrist for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I saw a psychiatrist in August, about the 15th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: And after that how many times did you see the psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: I go as needed, but once a month at least I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you were not in hospital. You just see the psychiatrist as an outpatient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not an in-patient in a hospital. There is no room. There are no beds. But I'm under his control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: And that control is every month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: It is every month or every 15 days or when I run out of medicaments or when I feel the consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Right now do you have a monthly control or in shorter intervals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MC3
utterances.text: Now it is a month, but I can go and see him before that date if I feel the difficult consequences. I can ask to see my doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miljevic. Ms. Sutherland, any need for further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness MC3, this concludes your testimony in this court. It's been a long way, and you've testified --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask a question, just one question, a very brief one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether I could give an answer to your question, but I'll allow you to put a question, but I'm not promising that we are able and we are in a position to answer the question since we do not know the question yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm only going to ask: Who is going to make good these violations of my security, of my health, of my condition? Who is going to pay that? Who is going to compensate that for me? Because he hurt us. He targeted us witnesses, as a war criminal, and that is still being done today. We came here to take the witness stand in an honest fashion, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to assure you that any violation of protective measures always is taken very seriously by this Tribunal. That, I take it, is also the reason why the Prosecution has started this prosecution, this prosecution which has not yet resulted in any judgement. That's also the reason why other cases have been prosecuted before this Tribunal, because the Tribunal takes these matters very seriously. As far as the practical question is concerned that who is going to compensate for it, I can't answer that question. The best thing you could do is to further discuss this with the victims and witness section. I cannot even say that there's any way of compensating for it, but certainly we could give no answer to that at this moment. Then I'd like to thank you again for coming to The Hague where I said before if there's a violation of protective measures that when I said that it's taken very seriously, that of course is, because it's general knowledge that if a witness testifies under protective measures that it will be very difficult for him to find out at a later stage that his protection was not effective. The Chamber is fully aware of that. You'll now be escorted out of the courtroom by Madam Usher. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have copies of Witness MC1's and MC2's statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reacted statements that you wanted to tender. Madam Registrar will receive them and assign a number to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these ... Madam Registrar, could you please, referring to dates and pseudonym of the witnesses, assign numbers to them. Perhaps we start with MC1. We have a statement MC1, the 16th of November, 2006. That would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then also MC1's statement, the 20th of November statement, same year.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move to MC2, one of the 16th of November, statement of 16th of November.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we have -- there's only one MC2 statement, or is there another one? I thought there would be two as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there should be two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another one of the 19th of November. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let me see. The Prosecution Exhibit 30 is the 16th of November, and then the statement of the 19th of November, MC2, would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 31, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much Madam Registrar. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you for doing my job, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't seem to have the statement of the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the Bench, finally, there's at least one copy of each statement. We'll very practically resolve this matter. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that completes the evidence for the Prosecution in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That completes the evidence for the Prosecution. Mr. Miljevic. Then it's now for the Defence to present its evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the materials that were provided to me by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, I received a decision, IT-95-14/2-RI77. The date is the 22nd of August, 2006, in the proceedings against Josip Jovic, where a decision was made that documents 18 be made confidential again and admitted into evidence. That was also attached in the table attached to the reports from the press conference of this Tribunal of the 23rd of August this year. In this same case, on the 11th of July, 2006, a decision was made that my client interpreted, and he still believes that from that date onward the list was no longer confidential. I think that all the requirements have been met here from Rule 68 that speak of the disclosure of exculpatory and other materials. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, may I interrupt you for a second. You're talking about documents which are not in evidence at this moment. So it may have been disclosed to you, but in the proceedings before this Tribunal not all the documents given to you are available to the Bench. So therefore, if you would like us to pay attention to these documents, you should introduce them into evidence. Have you copies for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I'm talking about. That is what I've just said. That was submitted to me, not disclosed to me, and I would like to have this admitted into evidence. Whereas I do have copies for you, here, in the English language. I have them and I would like to submit them straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you give them to Madam Usher, then ... May I take it that the Prosecution is familiar with these documents or not at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we're familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So even if there may be no copies for you at this moment that would not prevent the Chamber from proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We're aware of the 22nd of August decision and the 23rd of August press release, but we do not know about the decision on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miljevic, I see at this moment before me one copy with some underlining added, copy of a decision dated the 22nd of August, 2006, a decision by Trial Chamber III. I also have in front of me a press release, but I have not yet a July decision, although it may be -- let me just -- no. No reference is made to any July decision. Could you provide us also with the decision of -- you said the -- the 11th of July. Have you got a copy of that decision for us as well? Yes. Could you provide it to Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I received these documents from the OTP, they hadn't been disclosed until now. I suggested that they be disclosed and admitted into evidence. But what I would like to ask for now is what I had already asked for during the course of the proceedings today, the application of Rule 126 bis and 127. Since I got the documents after the 24th of November, we are still within the time-limit of 14 days, according to 126 bis. So we still have six or seven days left, so could I kindly be allowed to submit the document within those six or seven days?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rule 126 bis provides for the time need for filing responses to motions. I do understand that material was disclosed to you. Disclosure is not a motion. Do you say -- is it your position that since you received this material rather late that you cannot provide it to the Chamber? I thought -- I was under the impression that it served the interests of the Defence if the Chamber would have that decision on its table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you are quite right, because I actually did refer to Rule 68, and that is the discovery of exculpatory and other materials. I believe that that document would be extremely useful for the defence of my client, and that is why I'm kindly asking to have permission to disclose it as soon as possible, but so far I haven't been in a position to do so because I got it only after the 24th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this mean that you just don't have the document at this moment with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can submit it to the Court within 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Prosecution assist the Defence in this respect? Is there any possibility that within the next 20 minutes the Prosecution could provide a copy of that document so that it's handed over to -- is that possible or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if the Defence can give more details. Is it a written or oral decision, and is it in the Jovic case on the 11th of July, 2006?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. According to my information, it is one and the same case, and I referred to it already, the number I mentioned a few moments ago, and the date of the decision is the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you know whether it's a written decision or whether it's an oral decision? I can't imagine that it's -- if it's about admission of evidence that it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll do a search on the transcript for that date and through the JDB for a written decision on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since I do understand from the second decision that it has got something to do with Exhibit 18, and perhaps the second decision ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 11th of July, Your Honour, is the date of the actual hearing, so perhaps there was an oral decision made during that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's any way for you to search in the transcript and find the relevant portion, then it certainly would assist the Chamber in having this. We're all trying to do our utmost best to get that decision on our table as soon as possible. Mr. Miljevic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are the only two documents that I would like to have admitted into evidence in writing, but my client is also prepared to testify in his own case, once this document is admitted into evidence, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, that he's prepared is fine, but either you call him or you don't call him. It's up to you what evidence you want to present. Therefore, do you want to call your client as a -- do you want to call the accused as a witness in his own case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as it was mentioned here today, I was asked yesterday during the informal meeting whether my client would be prepared to testify in his own case, and I said yesterday what I'm saying here today. That is to say, that my client does wish to testify in his own case but only once this document has been admitted into evidence, because I believe that that is going to be the backbone of his defence in relation to Rule 77, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the situation the Chamber wanted to avoid, we are now in a situation where we have to adjourn. We can't continue further today. Due to understandable reasons for Defence counsel we can't continue tomorrow. So therefore we are now in a situation where the Defence wants to call a witness, that is the accused, and at the same time relies on what the Defence calls a document but what we understand at least is a decision which may be contained in a transcript. It's not the way the Chamber expected the case presentation of the Defence to be. At the same time, it seems to be this decision, and perhaps the testimony of the accused might be of importance for the case, and therefore the Chamber sees no alternative than to adjourn to have this last part of the presentation of the Defence case, to hear that at a later date and then immediately after that to hear closing argument, because in contempt cases final briefs are not envisaged. We can't give you a date yet when we will resume, but we'll try to have that as soon as possible. And, Mr. Miljevic, you're invited to communicate with the Prosecution and also to communicate with the registry as to your availability and then we'd like to see you back at the date when we resume. I'm now informed that there may be a possibility to continue this afternoon since the Mrksic case will take less time, although there are some other logistical problems as well which have to be resolved before we continue. I suggest that we have a break of 15 minutes at this moment, that the Prosecution tries to find the relevant portion of the transcript in which the decision is contained, then communicates that to the Defence and then we'll see if we could still continue this afternoon. We stand adjourned for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miljevic, has the work performed during the break resulted in anything the Chamber has to hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't know. I have been informally informed by the OTP that they have the hearing transcripts, a part of them that is, but I haven't seen them, so I don't know what they contain, actually. My client still maintains that it was the 11th of July. Whether that is so in the transcript in reference to that particular date I have no way of knowing. I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's, of course, part of the preparation that should have been done. This means that in the present situation do you want to call your -- the accused as a witness? Perhaps he could clarify. I don't know whether there's anything he could tell us about it, but we gave you ample time and you were assisted by the Prosecution. I take it that the Prosecution then has searched the transcript of the 11th of July hearing, and do I understand that nothing was found on admission of lists?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We did an electronic search on the word list, Exhibit 18, and then printed out a hard copy of the transcript which we then tried to quickly review as soon as possible. It's 118 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The whole transcript is in open session. I don't see any private session. We've also searched for that word electrically, to see whether in fact there is any private session. And then I was going to provide the whole transcript to Mr. Miljevic to see himself whether there's anything that he finds of relevance in the transcript, but we only just finished reviewing the transcript ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miljevic, everyone worked hard to see whether they could assist you in procuring the evidence you'd like to present and which is not at this moment available from what I understand. Nevertheless, you provided us with the 22nd of August decision, which may shed some light on the matter as well. How would you like to proceed with the presentation of the Defence case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the decision of the 22nd of August was admitted into the file as well as the press release from the press conference of the 23rd of August where the list of -- the list actually indicates that it was on that date that such a ruling was passed, after that I only intended to obtain this exhibit which obviously we could not do today, and then after that my client be examined as a witness in his own case. Therefore, I should like to ask this Tribunal, if that is at all possible, after we have adjourned -- to proceed in that way after we have adjourned for a couple of days because we are really exhausted, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber might take one or two minutes to deliberate, but first we'd like to hear from the Prosecution whether they -- what their position is in respect of adjourning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's our position that the case should continue today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's short and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for two minutes. --- Break taken at 3.09 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue at stake, it appears from other material and evidence, is known to the Defence for quite some time, so they have had ample opportunity to find any document or any transcript which would cover the matter. At this moment, the Chamber sees no reason to adjourn. Whether we would at a later stage is a different matter, but we invite you, Mr. Miljevic, to proceed at this moment. That means either to present other evidence or to call your client as a witness, to call the accused as a witness in his own case. Please tell us how you wish to proceed at this moment. If you want to consult with Mr. Margetic, of course you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was firmly promised that this hearing today would last until 2.00 or 3.00 at the most. That is why I came here. But the situation being as it is, I have no option but to proceed, and I propose to call my witness, to examine him as a witness in his own case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Margetic, you're called to the stand. Madam Usher, could you ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetic, before I'll invite you to give a solemn declaration I'd like to -- one second, please. Please sit down for a minute. It should be clear to you that you are under no duty to testify in your own case. You may remind silent. But once the Defence has decided that you do testify in your own case as a witness, then you're under an obligation to answer all the questions, to answer them truthfully, also to answer any questions that will be put to you in cross-examination by the Prosecution. If you would not speak the truth, then you may be prosecuted for perjury. You should be aware of that, that you're not under any duty to testify, but if you testify that it brings obligations and that it may have consequences. Mr. Margetic, I take it that you want to make a solemn declaration as a witness in your own case. Yes. Then Madam Usher will give you the text of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Margetic. Please be seated. Mr. Miljevic, you may examine Mr. Margetic as a witness in his own case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Margetic, will you tell the Bench when did the proceedings which were instituted before this court against you end and how?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: They -- it finished in the mid-June last year, and the OTP of the Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia actually dropped the case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can counsel please slow down. Because of the overlap the interpreter could not catch it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to -- you both speak the same language, so once you have put your question, Mr. Margetic should wait until it has been translated into English. He can see when it still moves on his screen it's not there in English yet. Wait and then give the answer. Similarly, Mr. Miljevic, you will have to wait after Mr. Margetic has given his answer a while before you put your next question to him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Bench whether you remember if in April of this year you received any order from the OTP or any communication whatsoever in respect of the fact that you were bound by confidentiality and had to keep secret in relation to the witness list in the Blaskic case?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: No. No, I never received any similar communication, nothing of the kind. And in the beginning of May, if I remember correctly, I received in -- in an envelope, a mail dispatching envelope, I received a CD with Tribunal materials, and the CD -- on the CD was written by hand "disclosure," and the number of the file, so that at that particular moment I thought that this was material that had already been disclosed and from which the mark of confidentiality had been lifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Could that have been on the 12th or 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: It may have been. It's around the middle of May more than anything else. I don't really remember, because I receive mail quite often and a lot of it, so I believe that it was around the -- around mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have your own ports or your internet domain where you publish certain things and, if so, what is it?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: The only web page which I use was www.domagojmargetic.com. At this moment, I am using the blog to write, but I'm not discussing any topics associated with this. I'm writing about the situation, the internal political -- regarding the internal political scene in Croatia and its economy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Bench when was it that you published this list of witnesses who were protected witnesses in the Blaskic case? Did you do that and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: Yes, in May after I had received this CD on which it was written "disclosure." Frankly speaking, I thought that that in a way was a sort of provocation of me as a journalist in order to actually prompt me to publish confidential material, and at that point I did not wish to publish it. And as we all know, for two months, a bit more than that, I actually did not publish this document at all. However, in mid-July, I came across a decision published on the internet. It was a decision in the case against my colleague, Mr. Josip Jovic, and the gist of it was that this list -- that those lists, in fact, in the case against Mr. Jovic had been already made public as an exhibit and the number of the exhibit was 18. It was a public exhibit. And at the time I thought that this was really a public document, a document in the public domain, because this is indeed what happened with the witness in the same case. And I thought that the Trial Chamber, in the case against my colleague Mr. Jovic, as it had in my case earlier, decided to lift the protective measures for those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Which witness are you referring to who had his protective measures lifted?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: In a previous trial we were indicted for violating the protective measures against Stjepan -- imposed on Stjepan Mesic, the president of Croatia, and in the course of the trial the protective measure was lifted in his case, and I thought that in the case of my colleague Mr. Jovic the Trial Chamber had actually done the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: Would you have published this list had you not seen this information on the internet?

utterances.speaker: DOMAGOJ MARGETIC
utterances.text: I would like to tell the Chamber for two months I did not publish this list. I had the list in my possession. Had I wanted, had it been my intention to endanger those witnesses in any way, to commit contempt of court, I would have done it in those two months. After this decision on the 11th of July, I believed that the Court had decided that, and this can be seen from the decision of the 22nd of August.
